summary: New Jersey is strict about exotic pets in general, but it expressly exempts the entire rat genus: its exempt-pet list (N.J.A.C. 7:25-4.4) names 'Mice and Rats, Mus spp. and Rattus spp.' Because the exemption is written at the GENUS level, it covers Rattus rattus exactly as it covers the common fancy rat. So keeping and breeding a captive-bred roof rat is legal with no exotic/nongame permit (just cage it to prevent escape and never release it). Private rehoming/adoption is fine; COMMERCIAL selling triggers Fish & Wildlife pet-shop/dealer licensing. No pet-rat-specific state import certificate was found (the CVI rules cover livestock/poultry).

keep.why: N.J.A.C. 7:25-4.4(a) lists species that 'may be possessed in this State without a permit,' and subsection (a)2.v lists 'Mice and Rats, Mus spp. and Rattus spp.' Because the exemption names the entire genus Rattus, captive-bred Rattus rattus falls within it and needs no exotic/nongame possession permit. The only condition (4.4(b)) is that the animal be caged to prevent escape. Rattus is absent from the permit-required list (7:25-4.3) and the potentially-dangerous-species list (7:25-4.8). Gemini DR-verified: N.J.A.C. 7:25-4.4 exempts the entire genus Rattus from exotic-wildlife permitting (the model genus-level exemption).

breed.why: An exempt species under 7:25-4.4 is removed from the possession-permit scheme, and no NJ Fish & Wildlife rule imposes a hobby-breeding permit for an exempt pet rodent. Breeding is simply continued possession of exempt animals, so long as the no-escape housing rule (4.4(b)) is met and animals are never released (N.J.S.A. 23:4-63.3). Commercial-scale breeding for sale shifts into dealer/pet-shop licensing. Gemini DR-verified: no statewide hobby-breeder license for exempt rodents.

sell_give.why: Because Rattus spp. is exempt, transferring or giving an individual pet rat is not barred by the possession code. But anyone SELLING exotic/nongame wildlife commercially must hold the applicable NJ Fish & Wildlife permit, a Pet Shop–Retail Sales permit or an Animal Dealer–Wholesale permit ($100 each). Free adoption/rehoming via private transfer is the cleanest route and avoids the dealer question. Gemini DR-verified: private giving is unregulated; commercial sale needs a MUNICIPAL pet-shop license (local health dept), not a state exotic-dealer permit.

transport.why: Intrastate transport of a lawfully-possessed exempt pet is not restricted. New Jersey's animal-import / CVI scheme (N.J.A.C. 2:3) is limited to livestock and poultry and does not impose a CVI on pet rodents. The binding statewide rules are the no-release prohibition (N.J.S.A. 23:4-63.3) and the no-escape caging rule (7:25-4.4(b)). Confirm import expectations with the State Veterinarian, as no rat-specific rule was located. Gemini DR-verified: intrastate unregulated; import of companion rodents isn't subject to a state CVI (livestock/poultry/dogs-focused) - a practical-legal gray area; commercial carriers may still require a CVI.
transport.governing_law: N.J.A.C. 2:3-1.2/1.4 (livestock/poultry CVI, excludes pet rodents); N.J.S.A. 23:4-63.3 (no release); N.J.A.C. 7:25-4.4(b).

restrictions.summary: Selling pet rats COMMERCIALLY requires a NJ Fish & Wildlife permit, a Pet Shop–Retail Sales permit (selling to individuals) or an Animal Dealer–Wholesale permit (selling to stores), $100 each, with recordkeeping. Private free adoption/rehoming does not.
steps: For commercial sales: obtain the appropriate NJ Fish & Wildlife pet-shop/dealer permit
